session_check: bmo. The issuer's own 18 Sep 2026 Ad-hoc says the 9M report 'will be published as scheduled on 27 October 2026'. The last three results releases went out at 08:00 CET/CEST: Q3 2025 on 23 Oct 2025 (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/villeroy-boch-holds-its-own-in-a-challenging-market-environment/c73c6ff0-b535-4afd-83cf-00d0eda15bd3_en), Q1 2026 on 12 May 2026 and H1 2026 on 30 Jul 2026. There is no timestamp for 27 Oct itself because the IR Finanzkalender is behind a Cloudflare challenge, so this verdict rests on the issuer's pattern.
positioning_check: Bundesanzeiger Netto-Leerverkaufspositionen register read as of 2026-10-23, no position for this issuer: the 0.5% truncation floor, not a measured zero (anchor_covered false). Building or covering is unknowable from it, and priced_lean_pct is effectively the run-up. Tape: -20.6% from the 18 Sep close (14.35) to 11.40, SDAX +1.5% and Geberit +6.0% over the same span, no company news since 21 Sep.

findings.finding: The new guide implies H2 2026 operating EBIT of only EUR 15.5-21.5m (FY 50-56 less H1 34.5) against EUR 50.0m in H2 2025 (Q3 17.3 + Q4 32.7). Even with a near-zero Q3, the implied Q4 of about EUR 10-20m is 40-70% below Q4 2025, which already excluded the divested Gustavsberg business. Against that, the H1 order book was up EUR 49.5m. So a confirmation, or a pointer to the upper half, is more likely than a fourth cut, though the Q3 headline will look ugly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: First 2026 guide at FY results 19 Mar 2026: -7.1% on the day (Yahoo closes). Guide to lower end, 12 May 2026: -3.5%. Guide confirmed, 30 Jul 2026: -1.0%. Cut on 18 Sep (ad-hoc, after hours): +0.7% the next session, then a grind lower.
findings.why_not_priced: The H2 arithmetic needs three releases combined (Q3 2025 statement, H1 2026, the ad-hoc) and no sourced sell-side update since the cut was found. But this company has cut three times in 2026, so the market may simply distrust the guide. If it had priced a credible guide, the pref would not have fallen 20% after the cut with no new news.
findings.independence: Same arithmetic, different documents: Q3 2025 9M op. EBIT 65.1m (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/villeroy-boch-holds-its-own-in-a-challenging-market-environment/c73c6ff0-b535-4afd-83cf-00d0eda15bd3_en) and the H1 2026 order book (https://www.eqs-news.com/news/corporate/villeroy-boch-navigates-a-challenging-market-environment-and-confirms-its-full-year-forecast/fb83e28b-09b7-438f-bd95-399e6329824c_en). Not independent of the guide itself.

findings.finding: The pref has fallen from EUR 14.35 (18 Sep close, before the ad-hoc) to EUR 11.40 (-20.6%), with no company news after 21 Sep, while the SDAX rose about 1.5% and Geberit about 6%. The only documented cause is the dividend-policy change, under which a near-zero group result means the EUR 0.13 statutory minimum per pref (Satzung para 3(3)) against EUR 0.85 for 2025. That points to yield holders having already exited before a release that most likely confirms the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of a pre-print capitulation on this name. Release days have mostly closed lower: 5 of the last 7 observed (2025-05 -3.3, 2025-07 -4.2, 2026-03 -7.1, 2026-05 -3.5, 2026-07 -1.0; up on 2025-03 +1.7 and 2025-10 +1.9).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced by construction, since this finding is the price. What it says is that the cut has been absorbed and more: the move (-20.6%) is close to the cut to the EBIT guide midpoint (-29%) and to the dividend falling 85%. If the market still had to price the cut, the pref would be nearer the EUR 13.7-13.9 it traded at on Tradegate the evening of the ad-hoc. Shrunk because a drawdown with no cause in the filings is worth about zero.
findings.independence: The dividend floor is from the company's Satzung (https://www.villeroyboch-group.com/fileadmin/user_upload/images/Investor_Relations/Finanztermine/Hauptversammlung/DE_SatzungVBAG_12052023__sec_.pdf, via search snippet only, because the IR host is behind Cloudflare). The SDAX and Geberit comparison is from Yahoo closes for ^SDAXI and GEBN.SW.

findings.finding: The release is likely to show a negative 9M group result (H1 was -EUR 6.8m). Under the 18 Sep policy ('no more than the Group's result ... distributed; in any event the minimum dividend will be proposed') that all but fixes the 2026 pref dividend at the EUR 0.13 statutory minimum, against EUR 0.85 for 2025.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend policy change came out with the 18 Sep ad-hoc; the pref fell about 20% over the following five weeks.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the policy has been public for five weeks and the H1 loss for three months. Kept small because the release may be the first document from which holders can read that the 2026 payout is the minimum.
findings.independence: The 2025 dividend of EUR 0.85 per pref comes from Börse Express, 19 Mar 2026 (https://www.boerse-express.com/news/articles/villeroy-boch-aktie-nahost-krise-bremst-880083).

findings.finding: Board member Esther Jehle bought EUR 83,330 of prefs at an average of EUR 13.89 on Tradegate on 18 Sep, after the 17:49 ad-hoc. That is about 18% above the current EUR 11.40.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier insider buys (Schupp in Mar 2026, Jehle in Dec 2025, Warncke in Aug/Sep 2025) preceded falls; no sign they predict release-day reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since 21 Sep and the price has fallen through it, so it is nearly fully priced. It counts only as a weak signal that the board did not expect the quarter to get worse after the reset.

'Understatement is systematic, size on what is new': abs_move_pct raised from 4.0 to 4.5, because Q3 numbers are not yet out and turnover is thin, though the guide was just reset
